messages.text: Venus Williams given US Open wild card - with another held potentially for Serena

metadata.summary: Venus Williams has been given a wild card into the US Open singles draw, and the tournament is keeping one on hold - perhaps in case her sister Serena wants to join her.
metadata.content: US Open: Venus Williams given Flushing Meadows wild card place in New York - with another spot held potentially for Serena | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open: Venus Williams given Flushing Meadows wild card place in New York - with another spot held potentially for Serena At the age of 46, Venus Williams given US Open singles wild card place; Tournament has also held back one further wild card place, potentially for sister Serena Williams - who made tennis return at Wimbledon; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis from August 30 Tuesday 18 August 2026 18:36, UK Image: Venus Williams (right) has been given a US Open wild card place, with another spot held back potentially for sister Serena (left) Venus Williams has been given a wild card into the US Open singles draw, and the tournament is keeping one on hold - perhaps in case her sister Serena wants to join her. Sloane Stephens, the 2017 US Open champion, was one of six other women to receive a wild card, and the US Tennis Association said the final one is still to be announced. That almost certainly would go to Serena Williams, if she decides she wants to return to the tournament at 44. Coverage of the US Open begins on Sunday August 30, live on Sky Sports Tennis. Venus received a wild card last year, returning to the tournament she won twice for the first time since 2023. metadata.summary: Barcelona have confirmed the signing of Rodri from Manchester City in a deal worth £65.4m.
metadata.content: Rodri transfer news: Barcelona complete £65.4m signing of Spain midfielder from Man City | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Rodri transfer news: Barcelona complete £65.4m signing of Spain midfielder from Man City Barcelona confirm signing of Rodri from Manchester City in deal worth £65.4m; the Spain midfielder has signed a four-year contract with the LaLiga club; City in talks to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi and remain interested in Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez Tuesday 18 August 2026 19:41, UK Image: Rodri has departed Man City for Barcelona Barcelona have confirmed the signing of Rodri from Manchester City in a deal worth £65.4m. The Spain World Cup winner and former Ballon d'Or winner, who helped City win four Premier League titles and a Champions League crown, has signed a four-year contract with the LaLiga club. Rodri, 30, had one year left on his City contract and, while they wanted him to stay and sign an extension, Barcelona's third offer proved to be too good to turn down. messages.text: Lakers governer Buss contesting siblings' plans to sell ownership stake

metadata.summary: Los Angeles Lakers governor Jeanie Buss is contesting her siblings' plans to sell the family's remaining 17.8 per cent ownership stake in the team.
metadata.content: Los Angeles Lakers: Jeanie Buss contests siblings' plans to sell ownership stake to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger | NBA News | Sky Sports Skip to content Los Angeles Lakers: Jeanie Buss contests siblings' plans to sell ownership stake to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger agreed a deal to buy the controlling interest in the Los Angeles Lakers at a valuation of $12.5 billion (£9.3bn) - a record for a professional sports team Tuesday 18 August 2026 16:35, UK Image: Jeanie Buss has been governer of the Los Angeles Lakers since 2013 Los Angeles Lakers governor Jeanie Buss is contesting her siblings' plans to sell the family's remaining 17.8 per cent ownership stake in the team. Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger agreed a deal earlier this month to buy the controlling interest in the Lakers at a valuation of $12.5bn (£9.3bn) - a record for a professional sports team. Kushner and Iger are reportedly buying about 65 per cent of the team from Mark Walter, who also owns a stake in baseball's Los Angeles Dodgers along with Chelsea chairman Todd Boehly. They would own about 83 per cent if they also reach a deal with the Buss family. The British-born Thai driver's current deal had been set to expire at the end of 2026, but has now secured his future ahead of the sport resuming after its summer break with the Dutch Grand Prix this weekend. Albon has scored just five points during the opening 11 rounds of the season, with Williams performing well below expectations after the introduction of the new regulations at the start of this year. messages.text: O'Neill: Celtic should aspire to win the Champions League

metadata.summary: Martin O'Neill believes Celtic should "aspire" to win the Champions League ahead of their play-off round qualifier against Austrian champions LASK.
metadata.content: Champions League: Martin O'Neill says Celtic should aim to win the competition as Arne Engels exit 'disappointment' discussed | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Champions League: Martin O'Neill says Celtic should aim to win the competition as Arne Engels exit 'disappointment' discussed Celtic take on Austrian champions LASK in the play-off round of Champions League qualifying; the Scottish champions were beaten at this stage of the competition last year by Kazakh side Kairat Almaty; qualification could land the club an estimated £40m By Adam Binnie Tuesday 18 August 2026 19:40, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manager Martin O’Neill believes Celtic should “aspire” to win the Champions League ahead of their play-off round qualifier against Austrian champions LASK. Martin O'Neill believes Celtic should "aspire" to win the Champions League ahead of their play-off round qualifier against Austrian champions LASK. The 74-year-old hailed the Lisbon Lions - who delivered the club's greatest ever achievement when they lifted the European Cup in 1967 - for "setting the bar" and wants his side to replicate their success despite the financial challenges of modern football. The Celtic manager also expressed his "disappointment" over losing influential midfielder Arne Engels to West Ham United just days before Wednesday's crucial £40m showdown.
